records.query: Need the patient's brain MRI (or CT) and EEG reports: MRI can reveal post-encephalitic gliosis or scarring supporting sequelae, while EEG assesses epileptiform activity underlying seizures; these are essential to confirm the hypothesis and exclude an occult structural lesion.
records.text:
Cranial CT:
      Title: Brain and Bone Window CT
      Description: Right cerebral hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia in right front and temporal lobe. Compensatory hypertrophy of temporal bone.
MRI:
      Title: Brain MRI (T1 FLAIR, T2WI horizontal and coronal)
      Description: Atrophy of right cerebral hemisphere and encephalomalacia of right frontal and temporal lobe
EEG:
      Description: Interhemispheric asymmetry with increased slow-wave activity in right temporal area, no epileptiform activity.

bindings.label: A 19-year-old male presents with headache described as blurred vision when hearing noise, followed by intermittent tingling at the top of the head, lasting about 5 minutes and occurring 5-6 times a day for the past 5 months
Past history includes encephalitis with high fever at age 5, followed by seizures at age 9; seizures were well-controlled with medication for the past 7 years
Patient became irritable with suicidal intentions a year ago and was diagnosed with anxiety disorder
Born at term with home delivery, normal physical growth (height 172.4 cm, weight 97.3 kg), no family history of mental illness or genetic disorders
Physical examination: right-handed male with symmetrical face and limbs, no abnormal walking gait; MMSE score 21 indicating mild mental retardation
CT and MRI show right cerebral hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia in the right frontal and temporal lobes
EEG shows right temporal slow waves without epileptiform discharges
Episodes are active focal seizures originating from the right temporal lobe
